title: GPU Died. Training Didn't: Self-Healing Training at Scale — Crusoe
talk_summary: Crusoe describes running Slurm on top of Kubernetes so that GPU node failures are detected and remediated automatically, with jobs requeued and resumed from checkpoints. The core mechanism is a failure-detection-to-replacement pipeline that cordons/drains bad nodes, swaps in healthy ones from spare capacity, and restarts the workload without human intervention.

takeaways.technique: Automatic node quarantine and replacement on failure detection
takeaways.what_they_do: On a critical hardware error, the system marks the node down, cancels running jobs, cordons and drains the Kubernetes node, removes it from the pool, and replaces it from spare capacity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the Kubernetes node is then cordoned and drained. And then the unhealthy node is removed from the node pool and replaced with a new healthy node from spare capacity
takeaways.numbers: ~5 minutes from detection to healthy node back in pool; <15 minutes total downtime end-to-end

takeaways.technique: Graceful termination window with checkpointing before kill
takeaways.what_they_do: Before terminating a job, the process gets a SIGTERM and up to two minutes to save checkpoints or flush logs; the cancelled job is then automatically requeued.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have up to two minutes to handle that sig term to either save your checkpoints or flush your logs before that node is eventually replaced

takeaways.what_they_do: When a node goes down, the running job is cancelled but automatically requeued so it resumes once a healthy node returns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The cancel job is automatically reued and then autoclusters start.

takeaways.technique: Opt-out label to protect nodes from auto-replacement
takeaways.what_they_do: Before replacing a node, the system checks that no pod on it carries a label disabling automatic replacement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it verifies that no pods on the node have a label that disables automatic replacement

takeaways.technique: Unified resource pool with dynamic reallocation
takeaways.what_they_do: Putting all GPUs in one cluster lets them move hardware between training and inference as load shifts, instead of idle capacity sitting in a separate static partition.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when your user uh load goes down, you have all these GPUs sitting idle. That's the perfect time to up your training job

takeaways.technique: Log every remediation for later reference
takeaways.what_they_do: Each alert and the remediation taken is recorded so users can review what happened without acting on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a record of the alert and the remediation is logged for the user's reference
